name: Fracture — Anti-Reputation Decentralized Net
description: Fracture is a deliberately decentralized counter-reputation network that runs on distributed Shelf hardware — no central servers, no corponation hosting — designed to expose the manipulation and fabrication endemic to corporate-run reputation systems like Meridian Score. Launched in 2209 by the pseudonymous collective known as Splinter Cell Ocho, Fracture assigns users a 'Crack Rating' based on peer attestation, contradiction history, and verified whistleblower contributions rather than corporate compliance metrics. The platform's core philosophy, encoded in its founding manifesto called The Break, is that reputation systems designed by power structures inevitably protect power structures — Fracture exists to make that visible.
cultural_impact: Fracture has become the primary tool by which Shelf journalists, labor organizers, and synthetic rights advocates vet each other before collaborating on sensitive actions — its Crack Rating is widely trusted in low-tier communities as a more honest indicator of character than any corporate score. Corponation security firms have spent significant resources attempting to infiltrate or spoof Crack Ratings, making the platform's peer attestation system a constant evolutionary arms race.
key_figures: The Node Called Vesper (E.L.F. infrastructure maintainer)
locations: Distributed across Shelf hardware clusters, no fixed address
The Cracked Mug, Tier 1 social hub used for in-person attestation ceremonies
Underworld mirror nodes, location rotates weekly
story_hooks: A Tier 4 corporate compliance officer discovers their Crack Rating on Fracture is catastrophically low — someone has been building a peer-attested case against them for years, and the evidence is about to go public in a form no corponation lawyer can suppress.

Splinter Cell Ocho fractures internally when one member is revealed to have accepted corponation money, and the resulting civil war over the platform's integrity threatens to destroy the only trusted reputation system the Shelf has.

A synthetic being with no legal identity uses Fracture's peer attestation system to build enough verified reputation to negotiate with a Tier 3 housing collective — and the corponation that owns the building sends a team to unmake that reputation before the deal closes.
user_base: Approximately 890,000 active nodes; predominantly Tier 1-2 residents, labor organizers, synthetic rights advocates, investigative journalists, and Underworld-adjacent operators who distrust corporate platforms
monetization: No monetization — infrastructure costs covered by voluntary hardware contribution from users running distributed nodes; occasional anonymous donations from Tier 3-4 sympathizers routed through Underworld channels
notable_feature: Crack Ratings cannot be purchased, appealed to any central authority, or algorithmically manipulated — they can only be changed by the same peer attestation process that built them, making Fracture the only reputation system in M88 that is genuinely immune to corporate interference
